content.title: About
content.content: The “Chocolate Cola” soft drink combines the classic cola taste with notes of milk chocolate. It contains water, sugar, caramel color, flavorings, caffeine and natural chocolate extract. The result is a sweet, slightly bitter aftertaste with characteristic fizz.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate‑flavored cola appeared in the early 2000s as a limited edition.
The cola‑chocolate combo is especially popular in Japan, where such flavors are common in vending machines.
A hint of vanilla is often added to soften the overall flavor profile.
Caffeine content is usually about 30 mg per 100 ml, comparable to regular cola.
The drink is frequently used in cocktail mixes, such as the “Chocolate Fizz.”

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugar and caffeine provide a quick rise in energy, useful for moments requiring heightened alertness.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Chocolate aroma stimulates serotonin production, helping improve mood.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like any soft drink, it contributes to overall fluid intake.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Regular consumption can lead to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Caffeine‑sensitive individuals may experience insomnia, rapid heartbeat, or anxiety.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Carbonated drinks can cause heartburn or stomach discomfort in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled, straight from the bottle or a glass. Pairs well with ice cream, desserts, and works as a base for mixed drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the cap tightly sealed to preserve carbonation.
